hints: Focus on which functional groups in santonin will change, remembering sodium reacts only with O-H groups in alcohols and carboxylic acids.
Look carefully at the left six-membered ring for C=C bonds and at the five-membered lactone, warm dilute acid will open the cyclic ester to give one -OH plus one -COOH.
Remember cold dilute KMnO4 adds two -OH groups across each C=C, so add those new alcohols to the hydroxy-acid from step one to get the total.
walkthrough:
**Spot the reactive groups in santonin**

Santonin contains a ketone, a cyclic ester (a lactone), and two C=C double bonds in the left ring as part of a dienone system.

Sodium metal reacts with: $$\text{R-OH + Na} \rightarrow \text{R-ONa + } \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2$$ $$\text{R-COOH + Na} \rightarrow \text{R-COONa + } \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2$$

**Hydrolyse the lactone with warm dilute acid**

Warm dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ hydrolyses esters. The lactone ring opens with water to give a hydroxy-carboxylic acid.

$$\text{lactone + H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{warm H}^+} \text{HO-R-COOH}$$
This creates 1 alcoholic -OH and 1 carboxylic -COOH, so 2 reactive H atoms so far. The ketone and alkenes are unchanged here.

**Dihydroxylate the alkenes with cold dilute KMnO4**

Cold, dilute, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ adds two -OH groups across each C=C to form a diol, it does not cleave the double bond and does not attack ketones or carboxylic acids.

$$\text{R-CH=CH-R' + [O] + H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{cold KMnO}_4} \text{R-CH(OH)-CH(OH)-R'}$$
With two C=C bonds, this gives $2 \times 2 = 4$ new alcoholic -OH groups.

**Count all O-H hydrogens in Q**

Product Q still has the original ketone, plus from step 2: 1 -OH + 1 -COOH, plus from step 3: 4 -OH.

Total alcohol -OH = $1 + 4 = 5$, plus 1 carboxylic acid = 6 O-H protons in total that react with Na.

options.A: 2 counts only the -OH and -COOH formed by lactone hydrolysis. It misses the four new -OH groups added when the two alkenes are dihydroxylated by cold KMnO4.
options.B: 4 comes from seeing only one C=C bond. If you add 2 -OH for one alkene to the 2 groups from hydrolysis you get 4, but the left ring is a dienone with two C=C bonds, so 4 -OH are formed, not 2.
options.C: 5 counts the five alcoholic -OH groups correctly (1 from hydrolysis + 4 from two alkenes) but forgets that the carboxylic acid -COOH formed on opening the lactone also contains an acidic H that reacts with sodium.
options.D: 6 is correct: 1 -OH + 1 -COOH from lactone hydrolysis plus 4 -OH from dihydroxylation of the two C=C bonds gives 5 alcohols + 1 acid = 6 hydrogens that evolve H2 with Na.
